Convert units

Source: R/convert.R
convert.Rd

A currency may carry a four-digit year – MEUR2015, MUSD2020 – because money is the one unit whose value moves in time. Converting between two currency-years needs an exchange rate and a price index, and the two can be applied in either order: deflating in the source currency and converting at the target year is not the same as converting at the source year and deflating in the target currency. The gap between them IS the change in the real exchange rate over the interval, and convert() warns when it is material.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'character'
convert(
  from,
  to,
  x = 1,
  database = "base",
  currency_route = "deflate_then_fx",
  basis = "gdp",
  from_year = NULL,
  to_year = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'numeric'
convert(
  x = 1,
  from,
  to,
  database = "base",
  currency_route = "deflate_then_fx",
  basis = "gdp",
  from_year = NULL,
  to_year = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'character,character,numeric'
add_to_convert(
  type,
  unit,
  coef,
  alias = "",
  SI_prefixes = FALSE,
  database = "base",
  update = TRUE
)

Arguments

from

character of length one with unit name

to

character of length one with unit name

x

numeric vector with data to convert

database

character name of a database with units (base by default, other options are not implemented yet).

currency_route

how to combine the exchange rate with the deflators: "deflate_then_fx" (the default) deflates in the source currency and converts at the target year, which is the World Bank and IPCC convention; "fx_then_deflate" converts at the source year and deflates in the target currency; "both" returns one value per route, named.

basis

which price index deflates, "gdp" (the default) or "cpi". Technology cost data is often published on a CPI basis.

from_year, to_year

the currency year, as an alternative to writing it into the unit. convert(1, "MEUR", "MUSD", from_year = 2015, to_year = 2020) is convert(1, "MEUR2015", "MUSD2020").

...

currently ignored

type

character, type of the unit (one of "Energy", "Power", "Mass", "Time", "Length", "Area", "Pressure", "Density", "Volume", "Flow Rates", "Currency").

unit

character, the name of the new unit to add to the database.

coef

numeric, convert factor to the base unit of this type (see the first column of convert_data[[database]][[type]]).

alias

character vector, alternative name(s) for the same unit.

SI_prefixes

logical, can be used with SI prefixes, FALSE by default.

update

logical; when the unit already exists with different values, TRUE (default) replaces them and FALSE raises an error instead.

Value

convert(): a numeric vector of converted values, or one value per route, named, when currency_route = "both".

add_to_convert(): invisibly, an updated convert_data ASSIGNED IN .GlobalEnv. The package's own data is not changed, and the assignment is lost with the session.

Details

A year is read only where the unit is a currency: MWh2020 is an unknown unit, not a dated one.

Money with no year on either side consults no price index and never warns – it is a pure exchange rate, read at currency_base_year(). That rate is generated from currency_fx at one stated base year; before version 0.93 it was typed in by hand and undated, with a euro rate from one year beside a yen rate from another, so untagged cross-currency answers moved once, at that release. A conversion within one currency – convert("EUR/kW", "MEUR/GW"), a ratio of prefixes – did not move and consults nothing.

See also

currency_fx and currency_deflator for the data behind a dated conversion, currency_base_year() and add_currency_fx() to read or extend it, and normalize_model_currency() to convert a whole model's costs at once.

Examples

convert("MWh", "kWh")
#> [1] 1000
convert("kWh", "MJ")
#> [1] 3.6
convert("kWh/kg", "MJ/t", 1e-3)
#> [1] 3.6
convert("cents/kWh", "USD/MWh")
#> [1] 10

# money with a year
convert(1, "MUSD2015", "MUSD2020")    # an inflation question
#> [1] 1.082839
convert(1, "MEUR2020", "MUSD2020")    # an exchange-rate question
#> [1] 1.142196
convert(1, "MEUR2015", "MUSD2020", currency_route = "both")
#> deflate_then_fx fx_then_deflate 
#>        1.241012        1.201424 

# the value first, which is the same call with the arguments the other way
convert(1000, "kWh", "MWh")
#> [1] 1
convert(5, "cents/kWh", "USD/MWh")
#> [1] 50
convert(1, "MEUR", "MUSD", from_year = 2015, to_year = 2020)
#> Warning: EUR2015 -> USD2020: the two routes differ by 3.3% (a factor of 1.033). Using deflate_then_fx.
#> The gap IS the change in the real exchange rate over the interval, so neither route is a rounding of the other.
#> Pass currency_route = "both" to see each, or raise options(energyRt.currency_route_tol=) to quieten this.
#> [1] 1.241012

# `coef` is the factor to the type's BASE unit, which is its FIRST column
# -- the joule for Energy, not the GJ or the MWh a modeller thinks in -- so
# a dekatherm (10 therms, 1.055 GJ) is entered as 1.055e9.
convert_data$base$Energy[, 1:4]
#>             J   Wh W*s  Cal
#> coef        1 3600   1 4187
#> SI_prefixes 1    1   0    0
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
add_to_convert("Energy", unit = "dekatherm", coef = 1.055e9)
convert(1, "dekatherm", "GJ")   # 1.055
} # }

# NOT the way to add a currency rate: a currency coefficient is generated
# from `currency_fx` at one base year, and overwriting one here would put
# it out of step with every other currency in the table. Use
# `add_currency_fx()`, which is dated and keyed by ISO code.
